payload.issue: docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md's Step 0b WF-2 SUPERVISED-HOLD check only recognizes two hold conditions on a resumed head.active_task_id row: effective_supervised (board/detail supervised flag) and the absence of a po_goahead_* stamp. It has no concept of a data-driven 'do not re-check before <timestamp>' hold that a specialist itself records mid-verification (e.g. a QA checkpoint that explicitly states the next re-check should not happen before a future time, because the verification window itself hasn't elapsed yet).

evidence.live_incident: FIX-MCP-SSE-SESSION-MANAGER-PERCONN-LEAK-NO-REAPER: qa's Step-5 checkpoint (field qa_step5_checkpoint_1_20260808T1832Z on the review[] row) explicitly recommended 're-dispatch qa for checkpoint #2 no earlier than 2026-08-08T21:00Z' because PO's own gate requires a >=4h sessionCount-vs-MemPerc correlation window that had only ~1h33m elapsed at write time. head.status stayed in_progress/next_agent=qa (correctly -- qa genuinely is the next real action, just not yet). On the very next dev-team tick (2026-08-08T18:37Z fire-election tick, ~19min later), WF-1/1b/1c all resolve task_status=empty (row lives in review[], outside their lookup array) and WF-2's should_hold evaluates false (no supervised flag, no po_goahead gate applies here) -- the mechanical S2 dispatcher-wrap would have re-claimed and re-spawned qa immediately, producing a checkpoint #2 that could only report the identical 'insufficient elapsed time' finding as checkpoint #1, wasting a full ~9min/130K-token qa agent run for zero new information. Declined to re-spawn this tick by manual judgment instead -- not a mechanized gate.
evidence.root_cause: WF-2's should_hold predicate (main.md ~L374-385) checks effective_supervised($detail_items) and a po_goahead_* key match -- it has no branch for a specialist-authored checkpoint field carrying its own recommended-not-before timestamp. Every tick between now and 21:00Z would hit this same wasteful re-spawn unless a human/router manually recognizes and skips it each time.

payload.impact: Any long-running, time-gated verification (a multi-hour correlation window, a soak test, a rate-limited external check) that a specialist checkpoints mid-flight with an explicit re-check-not-before recommendation will be blindly re-dispatched on every subsequent dev-team tick until the window closes, unless a human/router catches it manually each time (as done here). At dev-team's ~30min tick cadence, a 4h gate like this one would otherwise trigger ~7 wasted re-spawns before the window legitimately closes.
payload.requested_action: Extend WF-2's should_hold (or add a WF-2b sibling check) to also recognize a generic checkpoint-timestamp hold: if the resumed row carries any field matching a documented convention (e.g. ^qa_step\d+_checkpoint_\d+_ or a dedicated next_recheck_not_before ISO field) whose declared not-before timestamp is still in the future, hold (fall through to Step 1, head left unchanged, mirroring WF-2's existing supervised-hold behavior) rather than re-dispatching. Suggest standardizing on an explicit next_recheck_not_before field (any specialist can set it) rather than parsing agent-specific checkpoint-field-name conventions, so the gate stays agent-agnostic.
payload.occurrence_note: First observed instance of this gap. Not yet 2+ recurring, but structurally guaranteed to recur on this exact task (FIX-MCP-SSE-SESSION-MANAGER-PERCONN-LEAK-NO-REAPER) roughly every ~30min tick until 2026-08-08T21:00Z unless caught manually each time -- worth fixing before the next long-window verification task hits the same gap without a router present to catch it.
